pages.text: The river dropped so far that the water was distant. The yard's soil cracked. Water had to be used sparingly.
Each child planted seeds in a pot and set it in the yard beside the others. Mina crouched before their pot. A sprout would come up here.
Mom shared water in dippers. Mina looked at Raju's. "Raju's is bigger."
Mina set two dippers together to compare, narrowing their eyes.
Changing dippers, Mina tipped one over. Water sank into the cracked ground.
Three pots stood together. Raju's and Sonu's soil was dark and wet. Only Mina's was pale and dry.
Mina pressed the dry soil. It crumbled under a finger.
Mom touched the dry pot. "That ground drank all your water."
The next day, Mina poured gently from their own dipper. The soil grew dark and wet.
Days later, a pointed green sprout appeared. Mina brought their trunk close to look. It tickled.
